component.name: MousePods
component.summary: AirPods as a head tracker for Steam/Proton games

description.p: Reads the motion sensors of AirPods over Bluetooth and moves the in-game camera of TrackIR/FreeTrack games running through Proton, without opentrack. Per-game smoothing, ranges, calibration with points on your monitors and a neck model. Also works as a mouse.

screenshot.caption: Games page: tick a Steam game and its camera follows your head
3D cockpit demo: the view follows your AirPods, no game needed
Calibration: look at each point and hold still
Measured head angles, editable before saving

description.p: Everything MousePods reads from your AirPods, on the Labo page.

ul.li: Labo: a new "AirPods data" card shows what the earbuds themselves think of your motion (still, small movements, moving), the Bluetooth link quality, which earbud sends the head motion, the primary earbud, the audio source and the connected devices
Both earbuds' serial numbers (masked) and the hidden RemoteHID services, with the ones that stay silent
Read-only, no Bluetooth address is kept
Overview: the spatial audio card sits under the pictures again

Spatial audio: a "MousePods Spatial" output renders anything you play (music, videos, games, 5.1 and 7.1 films) in 3D in your AirPods, and the sound stays in place in the room while you turn your head
Intensity slider, width, head tracking on or off, and a test sound that walks around your head
The HRTF (MIT KEMAR, 1.1 MB) is downloaded on first use
The Flatpak now has access to PipeWire and the sound server for this

description.p: Games outside Steam, Star Citizen in one click.

ul.li: Games page: add a game outside Steam with its Wine prefix (Lutris, Heroic, Bottles, LUG Helper, plain Wine) and switch its head tracking on like a Steam game
Star Citizen and the other TrackIR "Enhanced" games get their table without switching them off and on
In the Flatpak, MousePods asks you to confirm a game outside Steam is closed before changing it

description.p: Much lighter with the window open, and a nicer overview.

ul.li: The overview no longer redraws itself 30 times a second: far less CPU, GPU and battery use while the window is open, and smoother
New overview: live head plot, battery rings, a head mouse card, your games with their Steam covers, and picture cards for the cockpit demo, the 360° player and simulators
The welcome guide no longer takes over when a page is asked for
New website look, matching the app

description.p: A new look and a new icon.

ul.li: New look in the GNOME style with MousePods orange, light and dark. The previous look stays available: Settings, Appearance, Classic
New overview: the live position of your head, battery, mouse controls, your games and quick links to the cockpit demo and the 360° player
Simpler sidebar: the main pages first, the rest under Advanced
Settings: appearance, language, start at login and notifications in one place
New app icon
Star Citizen and the other TrackIR "Enhanced" games (DCS, Elite Dangerous, ArmA, IL-2...) get head tracking through the game bridge. Games already switched on need to be switched off and on once
Option buttons no longer flick back after a click, and pause and resume can no longer end in the opposite state

description.p: The same app as 1.2.0, now on the stable Flatpak channel too (the 1.2.0 upload did not reach it).
Lighter on the CPU, more headsets, and a first step on Windows.

ul.li: The app and the controller use much less CPU while idle (app window: from about half a core to 4 % on NVIDIA)
The first calibration no longer crashes at the end on a fresh install
Other headsets, experimental: Sony WH/WF-1000XM5 and XM6, ULT Wear and Pixel Buds Pro through Android's head-tracker protocol
AirPods Pro 3 verified on hardware
Windows, experimental and from source only: the AirPods sensor stream through a test-signed driver, no mouse yet
Battery: an unknown level shows a dash instead of 255 %

description.p: Head tracking in games, a 3D cockpit, 360° videos and an app that updates itself.

ul.li: Games page: tick a Steam game running through Proton and its camera follows your head, no opentrack needed
Per-game profiles and a full-screen calibration that learns your head movement first
Built-in 3D cockpit demo and a 360° / VR video player, with side-by-side 3D for goggles
Browser extension: YouTube 360° videos follow your head on youtube.com
Desktop app with tray icon and first-run wizard, installed as a Flatpak with automatic updates
Interface in English, French and German

description.p: First release: head tracking from AirPods 3 and AirPods Pro on Linux, without an Apple device.
